prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a top-down egocentric view where the camera wearer stands above a rough ground surface (about 1.2 to 1.5 metres below) while holding the near edge of a large rectangular glass tabletop within arm's reach (0.3 to 0.8 metres away) in the lower-left foreground, with another person standing about 1.0 to 1.5 metres ahead in the upper-right holding the opposite edge. In the first two frames, the camera wearer's lower torso and left arm are brightly rendered in the bottom-left corner (0.2 to 0.5 metres away), while across frames 3 to 5 the glass pane is lifted closer to the camera (0.3 to 0.6 metres) and tilted, exposing the wearer's extended forearms and legs directly beneath the pane in the lower-left and a vertical post about 1.0 metre to the left in frame 5. The other person faces toward the glass and the camera wearer from the upper-right with their head cropped out of the top of the frame, while a third person's sandaled feet briefly appear on the ground at the bottom-right of frame 2 about 1.2 metres away. Unlike the RGB image—where the transparent glass visually merges with the sunlit ground, reflections, and body parts underneath—the depth map clearly isolates the tilted planar surface of the glass sheet and its sharp diagonal edge against the recessed background in frames 1, 2, 4, and 5. However, the depth map is unreliable on the transparent and reflective glass surface, particularly in frame 3 where the pane blurs into an indistinct gradient and in frames 1 and 2 where the second person's legs and the ground seen through the glass are flattened to the depth of the pane itself.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map detects only portions of the second person in the upper-right quadrant of frames 1, 2, 3, and 5, situated roughly 1.0 to 1.5 metres in front of and to the right of the camera wearer across the ~1.0-metre-wide glass sheet. In the RGB context, this person faces toward the camera wearer with their upper torso and head out of view above the top border, holding the far-right edge of the glass within their arm's reach while the camera wearer holds the near-left edge within 0.3 to 0.6 metres. As the two people shift and lift the glass from left to right across the 5 frames, the segmented masks track the second person's torso and arms in the upper-right of frames 1 to 3 and their right-side torso and legs in frame 5, though they completely miss the person in frame 4. While the segmentation masks help separate fragments of the second person's dark clothing and limbs from the dark background and blue-tinted glass overlay in frames 1 to 3, the map provides almost no scene layout information compared to the RGB strip. It is highly unreliable overall: it fails to segment the camera wearer's own body and arms in the lower-left, misses the third person's feet at the bottom-right of frame 2, fails to detect the large glass pane or any background structures, and splits the second person into fragmented, overlapping `person` instances where the glass occludes their legs in frames 1 and 3.
descriptions.pose: The body and hand skeleton map is completely black across all 5 frames, failing to detect any body or hand keypoints in the scene. From the RGB strip, the scene actually contains the camera wearer in the lower-left foreground (with their torso at 0.2 to 0.4 metres and both hands reaching out 0.4 to 0.7 metres to grip and support the glass sheet from below), a second person 1.0 to 1.5 metres away in the upper-right facing the wearer while gripping the far edge of the glass with both hands, and a third person's lower legs at the bottom-right of frame 2 about 1.2 metres away. Across the 5 frames, the camera wearer's hands shift from gripping the near left rim in frames 1 and 2 to pressing flat against the underside of the glass in frames 3 to 5 as the pane is raised and rotated clockwise relative to the ground, while both the wearer's and the second person's heads remain out of view beyond the bottom and top frame boundaries. Because it outputs no skeletons at all, the pose map adds no spatial information beyond the RGB image and is completely unreliable due to severe self-occlusion, top-down foreshortening, truncation of heads and torsos at the image borders, and visual distortion from the semi-transparent blue glass occluding the hands and limbs beneath it.
